Not every dog can do this, and not every trainer can or should. With the owners' permission, I used Bishop to help communicate a lesson to Ryder. Dogs naturally understand other dogs better than they understand us. The goal wasn't to make Ryder love every dog she sees-it was to teach her that she doesn't need to react to every dog she sees. Before training, a simple neighborhood walk was nearly impossible. Seeing another dog meant lunging, pulling, and trying to start conflict. Through obedience work and carefully controlled sessions with Bishop, Ryder learned a valuable lesson: not every dog is a threat, and not every situation requires a reaction. Also notice how Bishop's corrections increase in intensity throughout the video. He starts with the minimum amount of pressure necessary and only escalates when Ryder chooses not to listen. That's how dogs naturally communicate with one another. Will I tell these owners to take her to a dog park and expect her to be everyone's best friend? Absolutely not. But can we give her a better quality of life by helping her calmly walk past another dog across the street? Absolutely. Not every dog needs this type of training, but some dogs can benefit tremendously from it. I believe everyone should film their training videos and look back to see what they did wrong even if you don't post it. He graduated from Stanford's math department in three years and three months. His textbook series, Neuron, sells over a million copies a year. Every November, South Korea pauses for a single nine-hour exam called the Suneung. The Air Force halts training flights. For 35 minutes during the English listening section, no commercial flights can take off or land at Incheon, one of Asia's busiest airports. About 8,000 police officers escort late students on motorcycles with sirens running. Inside that exam, the most consequential questions are called killer questions. One of the biggest myths in fitness is that you have to lift heavy to build muscle. The research doesn’t actually say that. Study after study has found that light, moderate, and heavy weights can all produce similar muscle growth—provided you’re training with enough effort and getting close to muscular fatigue. Heavy weights are one effective way to do that, but they’re not the only way. In my opinion, the reason so many weightlifters and online trainers still say you can’t build muscle without heavy weights is because of how they’re taught. I know this because I am an NASM certified personal trainer. When you become a certified personal trainer, the education is centered around heavier weight lifting. You’re not taught a comprehensive system for building muscle primarily with lighter weights or bodyweight. That’s something I had to figure out through years of experimenting, studying the research, and seeing what actually worked in practice. So when you hear trainers insist that heavy lifting is the only way to build muscle, remember—they’re teaching the methods they were trained in. That doesn’t mean they’re the only methods supported by the evidence.  I’m a NASM certified personal trainer with a degree in exercise and 15 years training experience. #pilates #barre #matpilates
